applies_why: The text weighs the challenger's seed/loins chain against the defender's woman-route chain, exactly the chain-against-chain collision this rule governs.
quote: the challenger's seed/loins chain is footed but does not name Joseph as the begetter
rule_words: the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side
room: Phrase weighed: 'does not name Joseph as the begetter'. Reading one: it is the retired stating-verse test, letting the absence of any verse naming Joseph in its own words hold back a chain the judge concedes is footed. Reading two: it is a footing observation, that the chain's support simply does not reach the begetter question. I chose reading one because 'name' is statement language set against conceded footing by 'but', so an absence of explicit statement, not a gap in support, is made to do the work.
why: The judge lets the absence of any verse naming Joseph as begetter weigh against a chain conceded to be footed, which is the stating-verse test K-C retires at a judge's seat for either side.
